title: Immunity works before the threshold
hook: Herd immunity needs 75% here. Does 60% immune do anything at all?

knows: R0 is the average number infected by one case in a fully susceptible population
doesNotKnow: that effective R = R0 x the susceptible share, so it falls smoothly as immunity rises

misconception: Immunity does nothing until the herd-immunity threshold is reached.
objective: The learner can explain that each immune person removes some of a case's chances to infect, so with R0 = 4 and 60% immune a case infects about 1.6 people, and the 75% threshold is just where R reaches 1.

claims.text: In a well-mixed population with perfect immunity, the number a new case infects is R = R0 x the susceptible share; with R0 = 4 and 60% immune, R = 4 x 0.4 = 1.6.
claims.source: Anderson R.M. & May R.M. (1991) Infectious Diseases of Humans, Oxford UP, ch. 4 (effective reproduction number). Arithmetic in Demo.tsx (rEff).

claims.text: With R0 = 4 the herd-immunity threshold is 1 - 1/4 = 75%, the immune share at which R reaches 1.

On the stage, 10 cases each meet 4 people they could infect (40 contacts); at 60% immune 24 contacts are immune and 16 are infected, and at 75% 30 are immune and 10 infected. Who is immune follows a fixed random order (seed 24, layout only, not chosen for a result) in which the 40 contacts hold evenly spaced places, so the immune share of contacts equals the town's at every 5% step: the picture shows the average case, not one random draw.
claims.source: Demo.tsx LAYOUT: each case's contacts are the cells 2 steps away; contact ranks floor((j + 0.5) x 390 / 40) for j = 0..39, other people shuffled into the remaining ranks, against an immune cut of 390 x share; for share 5k% exactly 2k contacts fall below the cut.

claims.text: The model is a made-up disease with random mixing and perfect, lasting immunity; real contacts are not evenly spread.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; stated in the question ('well-mixed'), on the stage ('Toy town') and in the reveal.

recall.question: In a well-mixed toy town a disease has R0 = 5. Half the town is immune. About how many people does a new case infect at first?
options: About 5: immunity does nothing below the threshold
recall.why: R = R0 x the susceptible share = 5 x 0.5 = 2.5; immunity lowers R long before the 80% threshold.
